title: NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer — A unified library of SOTA model optimization techniques like quantization, distillation, pruning, neural architecture search, speculative decoding, etc. It compresses deep learning models for downstream deployment frameworks like TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT, vLLM, etc. to optimize inference speed.
content:
NVIDIA Model Optimizer (referred to as Model Optimizer, or ModelOpt) is a library comprising state-of-the-art model optimization techniques including quantization, pruning, Neural Architecture Search (NAS), distillation, speculative decoding and sparsity to accelerate models.
[Input] Model Optimizer currently supports inputs of a Hugging Face, PyTorch or ONNX model.
[Optimize] Model Optimizer provides Python APIs for users to easily compose the above model optimization techniques and export an optimized quantized checkpoint. Model Optimizer is also integrated with NVIDIA Megatron-Bridge, Megatron-LM and Hugging Face Accelerate for training required inference optimization techniques.
[Export for deployment] Seamlessly integrated within the NVIDIA AI software ecosystem, the quantized checkpoint generated from Model Optimizer is ready for deployment in downstream inference frameworks like SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT, or vLLM. The unified Hugging Face export API now supports both transformers and diffusers models.

To install stable release packages for Model Optimizer with pip from PyPI:
pip install -U nvidia-modelopt[all]
Model Optimizer will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use.
To install from source in editable mode with all development dependencies or to use the latest features, run:
# Clone the Model Optimizer repository
git clone git@github.com:NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer.git
cd Model-Optimizer
pip install -e .[dev]
You can also directly use NVIDIA container images, which have Model Optimizer pre-installed:
- nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:<version>-py3
- nvcr.io/nvidia/nemo:<version>
- nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:<version>
Before pulling and using the container images, please review their respective license terms. Make sure to upgrade Model Optimizer to the latest version as described above. Visit our installation guide for more fine-grained control on installed dependencies or for alternative docker images and environment variables to setup.

Model Optimizer follows a structured approach to managing deprecated features:
- Communication: Deprecation notices are documented in the Changelog. Deprecated items include source code statements indicating deprecation timing, with runtime warnings issued upon use.
- Migration Period: Since Model Optimizer is still pre-1.0, we provide a 1-release (~1-month) migration period after deprecation. During this window, deprecated features continue functioning while issuing warnings.
- Scope: The policy addresses both complete deprecations (entire APIs removed) and partial ones (specific parameters removed while methods remain).
- Removal: Following the migration period, deprecated elements are removed in alignment with semantic versioning standards, potentially including breaking changes in minor version updates while Model Optimizer remains in 0.x.

report.summary: NVIDIA open-sources Model Optimizer, a unified library for quantization, pruning, distillation, NAS and speculative decoding that compresses models for faster deployment on TensorRT-LLM, vLLM and SGLang.
report.background: As large language and diffusion models grow to hundreds of billions of parameters, inference cost and latency have become the dominant deployment bottleneck. Memory bandwidth, not raw compute, usually limits throughput, so low-precision formats like FP8 and NVFP4 are now essential. NVIDIA first shipped TensorRT Model Optimizer inside its TensorRT ecosystem, then rebranded it to NVIDIA Model Optimizer in December 2025 and open-sourced it in January 2025. The library consolidates techniques that were previously scattered across research code and vendor tools, mirroring a broader industry shift from training-centric AI infrastructure toward inference optimization. It also reflects NVIDIA's strategy of keeping its hardware and software stack (Blackwell FP4, TensorRT-LLM, NeMo) at the center of model deployment while still supporting open serving frameworks like vLLM and SGLang.
key_points: Model Optimizer unifies quantization, pruning, neural architecture search, distillation, speculative decoding and sparsity behind one Python API. It accepts Hugging Face, PyTorch or ONNX models and exports optimized checkpoints, letting developers compose multiple techniques instead of stitching together separate research repositories.

It is tightly integrated with NVIDIA Megatron-Bridge, Megatron-LM and Hugging Face Accelerate for training-time optimization, and its checkpoints deploy directly to TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT, vLLM and SGLang. A unified Hugging Face export API now supports both transformers and diffusers models.

NVFP4 and quantization-aware distillation are headline features. A Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W4A4 NVFP4 + QAD tutorial reports up to 1.30x vLLM throughput over BF16 with 3.1x smaller checkpoints, while Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B NVFP4 claims up to 5.9x higher decode-heavy throughput than a 754B FP4 model while matching BF16 accuracy.

Real-world adoption is documented across customers: Adobe cut diffusion latency 60% and total cost of ownership 40% using Model Optimizer plus TensorRT; Domyn compressed Colosseum-355B to 260B; Bielik.AI built a 7B Minitron model 33% smaller, 50% faster and retaining 90% quality via pruning and distillation.

Installation is simple via pip, and ready-to-deploy checkpoints are published on Hugging Face. Note that the project is still pre-1.0, with a one-release migration window for deprecated APIs and possible breaking changes in minor versions.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Model Optimizer lowers the cost and complexity of serving large models, which directly affects cloud economics and hardware demand. It gives NVIDIA a standardized software layer that makes its GPUs more attractive for inference while still interoperating with open serving stacks like vLLM and SGLang. For developers, it replaces a fragmented set of research scripts with one composable library, shortening the path from a trained checkpoint to a deployable, quantized model. For regular users, the practical effect is faster, cheaper AI features and the ability to run capable models locally on consumer GPUs, especially Blackwell RTX 50-series cards with FP4 support. The main risk is ecosystem lock-in, since the best results may assume NVIDIA hardware.
report.tools: To follow up, watch TensorRT-LLM, vLLM and SGLang for deployment; Hugging Face Accelerate, Megatron-LM and NeMo for training integration; and Model Optimizer's own AutoQuantize, Puzzletron, Minitron, Medusa and QAD workflows. Install with 'pip install -U nvidia-modelopt[all]' or use NGC PyTorch, NeMo and TensorRT-LLM containers, which ship it pre-installed. Ready-quantized DeepSeek-R1, Llama 3.x and Nemotron checkpoints are available in NVIDIA's Hugging Face collection.
